title: Size-classed KV page binning with reclamation hints
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket implements a new KV cache allocation strategy that reduces fragmentation and improves GPU memory utilization for continuous-batching workloads. The approach introduces size-classed 'pages' (bins) for KV entries, a light-weight per-GPU page coordinator that opportunistically coalesces small free regions, and reclamation hints propagated from the serving runtime to prioritize compaction while preserving low tail latency.
background: Current KV cache allocation is a variable-sized slab-like allocator that suffers from external fragmentation under workloads with heterogeneous key/value sizes and varying sequence lengths. Continuous batching exacerbates fragmentation as long-lived contexts and short-lived requests interleave, causing memory to be unusable despite free slots. Prior tickets explored slab compaction and generational pools but introduced either high CPU overhead or unpredictable latency spikes.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce fixed-size page classes (e.g., 4KB, 16KB, 64KB, 256KB) to bucket KV allocations by typical footprint; 2) Maintain per-page free lists and a lightweight page state machine (active, partial, free) on the GPU; 3) Add reclamation_hint metadata on allocations so the runtime can mark entries as cold/evictable; 4) Implement a background coalescer that runs on a dedicated low-priority CPU thread per node to merge adjacent free pages into larger free units and produce hot-to-cold compaction plans; 5) Expose runtime-configurable thresholds for proactive compaction tied to batch-size percentiles to avoid interfering with P99 latency.
design_decisions: - Size classes chosen based on histogram of observed KV entry sizes from production traces; - Pages are aligned to GPU memory allocation granularity to keep kernel-friendly; - The reclamation hint is advisory and may be ignored when latency budget is tight; - Background coalescer is rate-limited and paused during high tail-latency windows; - Use async DMA copies for compaction to avoid blocking the main serving threads when supported by hardware.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests demonstrating allocation correctness across size classes
End-to-end benchmark showing >=15% reduction in GPU memory fragmentation metric on mixed workloads
P99 token latency increase <= 2% under steady-state and no regressions in throughput
Telemetry exposes per-page-class utilization, fragmentation ratio, coalescer activity, and reclamation hint hit rate
Rollout plan validated in canary with dedicated capacity
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature behind runtime flag; unit tests and microbenchmarks. Phase 2: Canary on 5% of production nodes with conservative thresholds. Phase 3: Expand to Dedicated pools; monitor fragmentation and latencies for 2 weeks. Phase 4: Default-on with adaptive thresholds and optional admin controls in Console.
telemetry: Emit metrics: kv_page_class_utilization_{class}, kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_coalescer_runs, kv_compaction_bytes, kv_reclamation_hint_hit_rate, kv_eviction_latency; Add traces for compaction events and sampling logs.
implementation_notes: - Collect size histograms from trace logs (query: kv_alloc_size_histogram) before choosing class boundaries. - Reuse existing KV allocation APIs where possible to avoid broad surface churn. - Keep GPU-side page metadata compact to fit L1 caches. - Provide tooling to visualize page maps in Console debug panels.
risks: - Coalescer causing unexpected CPU/GPU interference if not rate-limited; - Wrong size-class boundaries causing internal fragmentation; - Reclamation hints could be gamed or mis-specified by higher layers leading to premature eviction; - Hardware without async DMA will see higher compaction overhead.
mitigations: - Rate-limit coalescer and pause on latency signals; - Start with conservative class boundaries and iterate with telemetry; - Make reclamation_hint optional and audited; - Fallback path that uses in-place free-only reclaim without copies on older hardware.
dependencies_notes: Requires follow-up PRs: runtime flag gating, Console metric panels, and a small change to the batching router to emit eviction-advisory metadata with requests.
